tex_content.label: claim:limit-splits-as-cylinder
tex_content.html:
\begin{claim} \end{claim}[The blow-up limit splits as a round $S^2$ times $\mathbb {R}$] $(M_\infty ,g_\infty (0))$ is isometric to $(S^2,h)\times (\Ar ,ds^2)$, where $h$ has non-negative curvature. \end{claim}
Proof

↗ thm:splitting-theorem\sketch Rays from $x_n$ to the horn end and to its boundary have lengths tending to infinity and converge to two ends of the limit. The splitting theorem gives a product with a non-negative curvature surface; nonflatness makes that surface diffeomorphic to $S^2$.

□
